note: ⚠️ SNG-322 / CCODE-52. The threat ladder — how bad this is, IN THE WORDS A PLAYER MEETS, rather than a number they never see. FIVE BANDS, because the ladder has exactly one job that matters: to make the line where a fight can kill you VISIBLE AND NAMED. Fewer than five and the warned/unwarned line lands in the middle of a band; more than five and the bands stop being distinguishable in a sentence.
theLine: ⚠️ THE DECISION ERIK LEFT ME: the warned line sits between `hard` and `grave`. At `grave` and above, the encounter is declared lethal, `lethalOfferClamp` fires, and THE PLAYER IS TOLD AND OFFERED A DECLINE. Below it they are not. One line, stated once, and the ladder decides it rather than a flag hand-set per encounter — which was the whole point of CCODE-52.

bands.name: Beneath notice
bands.meaning: You will win. The only cost is time, and the only risk is looking foolish.

bands.name: An even thing
bands.meaning: A real contest you are expected to win. You may be hurt; you will not be killed.

bands.name: Above your weight
bands.meaning: You can lose this. Losing costs you something you will still be carrying next week — a wound that lingers, gear gone, standing spent.
bands.note: ⚠️ THE LAST BAND WHERE LOSING IS NOT DYING. This is where most encounters should sit.

bands.name: This can kill you
bands.meaning: Going down here means going down for real: incapacitated, and what happens next is not yours to decide.
bands.note: ⚠️ THE WARNED LINE. The name is the warning — it is not a mood word, it is a statement of consequence, and a player who reads it and continues has chosen.

bands.name: Nothing here is for you
bands.meaning: You are not the intended answer to this. Fighting it is not a hard fight; it is a decision to die.
bands.note: ⚠️ IT MUST EXIST SEPARATELY FROM `grave`, or the game has no way to say 'this is not a difficulty, it is a wall'. A player should be able to meet a legend at full strength and be TOLD that.

howItIsUsed.decidesLethalFlag: an encounter's `lethal` comes from its band, not from a hand-set field
howItIsUsed.decidesTheOffer: `warn: true` fires lethalOfferClamp — explicit choice plus a Decline option
howItIsUsed.pairsWithAggressorKind: ⚠️ BAND SAYS HOW LIKELY YOU GO DOWN; `aggressorKind` SAYS WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU DO. A `grave` beast and a `grave` assassin are equally likely to drop you and completely different afterwards — the beast moves on, the assassin finishes the errand and hides the body. Two dials, two questions, no overlap.

authoringGuidance: Most content should be `fair` or `hard`. If everything is `grave`, nothing is — the warning stops being information and becomes noise, which is the failure mode this ladder exists to prevent.
